title: Button input handler: screen ring + hold detection + SOS arming
description: Implement the universal button interaction grammar from spec 19 §4, §8, §9. Requirements: short-press=ring advance (§4), hold ≥2s=SOS arming on single-button hardware (§4/§8), hold ≥5s=factory reset path with confirm (§9), hold feedback mandatory within 500ms (§4 — priority 2 bug if missed). No menu system, no cursor, no list navigation, no double-press, no Vulcan combos. Dedicated SOS button=immediate arming with no hold. Screens advance on press only, never timers. Covers all tiers (E/O/H). Spans spec 19 requirements 8-30, 44-45, 54-56.
close_reason: DONE (worker8/heft). Implemented spec/19-device-ux.md §4/§8/§9 button interaction grammar in the ux subsystem: short-press advances the screen ring (§4); hold >=2s arms SOS on single-button hardware (§4/§8); hold >=5s opens the guarded factory-reset path (§9); hold feedback mandatory within 500 ms (§4, H-tier LED 4 Hz per §10); dedicated SOS button arms immediately with no hold. Architecture mirrors fplq.2: ux_button_core.c is a pure host-testable interaction engine (FSM + thresholds + event vocabulary + LED override enum, no GPIO) so the normative grammar is pinned by tests independent of hardware; ux_button_zephyr.c feeds debounced press/release from lichen_hal_button_get (ISR disables edge -> 25 ms debounce work -> 50 ms hold poll) and dispatches events plus the LED override, wiring into the §10 LED language from fplq.2. VALIDATION: host tests/ux_button passes 10 conformance cases under ASan/UBSan (ring advance on short press; feedback at exactly 500 ms; SOS arm at exactly 2 s with the LED taking over mid-hold; reset path at exactly 5 s; reset outranks SOS under workqueue stall; dedicated SOS immediate; sub-500ms tap advances; idle + NULL safety); ux_button_core.c + ux_button_zephyr.c compile clean for t1000_e/nrf52840 ARM; ux_led host suite still passes. 3x codereview ALL DELEGATED to kimi-k3 with full convergence loop: correctness pass 1 found 5 real defects (SOS LED never took over mid-hold; duplicate threshold events on release; SOS could arm after reset opened; GPIO interrupt armed before work items init -> UB; LED dispatch stomped JOINING/MESSAGE_WAITING blinks), correctness re-review verified all fixed and found 2 more (RESTORE clobbered pre-SOS state on the reset path; stale invariant comments), security PASS (no software/network path to SOS or factory reset — physical GPIO hold only; ISR-safe; debounce cannot fabricate hold time), edge-cases found 4 (RESTORE ledger vs SOS ownership across presses; boot-held button invisible; clock-skew underflow to spurious reset; non-idempotent start), edge re-review verified all fixed. Net: 9 distinct findings fixed and re-reviewed to PASS across the convergence loop. No new beads needed (all defects were in-diff, fixed before commit). Not pushed (driver sync cadence owns push).
